role: AI provider login/session hub + local capture API + extensible CLI — decoupled fork of Clear Glass, no NEXUS dependency

sse.description: broadcasts every /ingest live, to any connected client

auth.description: §CORS+CSP HARDENING 2026-07-24 — real, not optional in a fresh install: guardian-lite used to have zero authentication and wildcard CORS ('Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *'), which meant any origin on the machine could reach every route below. Now: every route except GET /health and OPTIONS requires header X-CGL-Token to match config.json's guardianLiteToken (generated by config.js's ensureGuardianToken() on first boot, via main.js and cli.js both). A request with a missing/wrong token gets 401 {ok:false, error:'missing or invalid X-CGL-Token'}. This check is server-side and applies to non-browser callers too (curl, another local process) — it is the real access control, not the CORS layer below.

cors.description: §CORS+CSP HARDENING 2026-07-24 — Access-Control-Allow-Origin is no longer '*'. The request's Origin header is checked against an allowlist built live from providers.js (https://<host> for every host in every provider's hosts[]) — echoed back only on a match, omitted otherwise, with 'Vary: Origin'. Preflight (OPTIONS) also answers Chromium's Private Network Access check: if the request carries Access-Control-Request-Private-Network: true, the response carries Access-Control-Allow-Private-Network: true — required before a public-origin page (any of the provider sites) is allowed to fetch a private-network address (127.0.0.1) at all, independent of CORS and CSP.

csp_bridge.description: §CORS+CSP HARDENING 2026-07-24 — see csp-bridge.js. Each provider window's own session gets its response Content-Security-Policy's connect-src directive widened (never stripped) to also allow the guardian-lite origin, via session.webRequest.onHeadersReceived, applied in main.js's openAccountWindow before the window loads. This is what actually lets gm-shim.js's fetch()-based GM_xmlhttpRequest reach 127.0.0.1 at all — without it, the provider site's own CSP blocks the request before guardian-lite's CORS headers are ever evaluated. Only applied to provider-window sessions, never the hub window (which talks to guardian-lite over IPC, not fetch — see cgl:ledger-* below).
csp_bridge.injected_global: window.__CGL_BRIDGE__ = {origin, token} — set by userscripts.js before the GM shim, on every provider page load/navigation, so userscripts (eravos-ai-bridge.user.js included) read the live origin+token instead of hardcoding either.

routes.description: table defaults to 'artifacts' if omitted; no fixed schema beyond a table name and a JSON object
real row counts per table actually in use, not a fixed list

ipc.description: Electron main<->renderer channels — the interaction surface guardian's own contract has no equivalent for, since guardian isn't an Electron app. contextBridge-exposed via preload.js as window.hub.*, never raw ipcRenderer in the page.

channels.name: cgl:get-status
channels.returns: full provider+account status, cookie-verified against real session partitions

channels.name: cgl:open-account
channels.description: null accountId mints a new one — the 'add another account' action

channels.name: cgl:get-config
channels.returns: full config object, real config.json contents

channels.name: cgl:restart-guardian
channels.description: stop+start with current config — used when Options changes port/enabled/retention

channels.name: cgl:ledger-query
channels.returns: real rows, newest first, from the live store

channels.name: cgl:ledger-tables
channels.returns: real table names in use, excluding 'settings'

channels.name: status-changed
channels.description: fired after any account/provider/config change so the hub re-renders without polling

custom_commands.contract: module.exports = { name, description, async run(args, api) }

userscripts.location: userData/userscripts/*.js, auto-loaded on every provider page load + in-page navigation
userscripts.guardian_scripts_note: full Clear Glass's own userscript-claude.js etc will load and run here — same format, same mechanism — but calls back to guardian/cortex only get real responses if something is listening on those ports, which this fork does not start on purpose

config.created: automatically on first boot (config.ensureConfigFile(), called by both main.js and cli.js) — real file exists from first run, not only after Options is opened and saved at least once

keys.guardianLiteRetentionLimit: number, default 0 (unlimited) — real, enforced cap per table, oldest rows trimmed by timestamp
keys.guardianLiteToken: string|null, default null until first boot — minted by config.js's ensureGuardianToken(), see auth block above. null only means 'not yet generated'; a fresh install always has a real value by the time guardian-lite actually starts listening.
keys.enabledProviders: {claude, chatgpt, gemini, perplexity: boolean}, all default true

session_isolation.mechanism: Electron session.fromPartition, one partition per (provider, accountId) pair
session_isolation.not_oauth: none of Claude/ChatGPT/Gemini expose a public third-party OAuth flow — this opens a real window to the real site and persists the session, it does not implement or simulate OAuth
